newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to impose monopoly controls on Coca-Cola.
newsitem.headline: Israel to impose monopoly controls on Coca-Cola.

text.p: Israel's anti-trust authorities will soon declare the domestic Coca-Cola bottler a monopoly in carbonated beverages and restrict its sales practices, industry sources said on Sunday.

David Tadmor, commissioner for restrictive business practices at the Industry and Trade Ministry, refused to confirm or deny reports he was preparing to impose limits on the Central Bottling Co, which also produces other soft drinks as well as Carlsberg and Tuborg beers.

But industry sources said Tadmor would bar the closely-held company from signing agreements with stores and restaurants that link sales of its Coca-Cola products to purchases of beer. The company has only a small share of the Israeli beer market.

The sources said the authorities would also bar any contracts offering individual customers discounts on condition they increased Coca-Cola sales. Industry analysts said such contracts often tempted customers to drop competing products in order to boost sales.
The sources said Central Bottling held far more than the 50 percent minimum of the local soft drink market that under Israeli law subjects it to anti-trust controls.
Central Bottling's two chief competitors are Tempo Beer Industries Ltd, which has the Israeli Pepsi-Cola franchise, and Jaf-Ora Ltd.
